scope: Final plan-only closure audit of PLAN.md, README.md, requirements traceability, the round-2 resolution register, all six round-2 reviews, all four round-1 resolution memos, and the repository-agent-operating-system evidence-repair/provenance artifacts. The removed prototype was treated as intentionally absent. No implementation proof was requested or inferred. I checked all 25 round-2 findings claimed addressed, the 52/52 round-1 root register, section and local-path references, R0-R4 vocabulary, authority ownership, roadmap numbering, normative conflicts, and ordered reader execution.
strengths: PLAN.md consistently labels the deliverable plan-only and explicitly says implementation, semantic evidence validation, production safety, and autonomous self-government are not proven.
The traceability counts reconcile: 16/16 user requirements, 52/52 memo-local round-1 roots, and 25/25 round-2 findings (15 high and 10 medium) are present in their registers.

Section 20 is the sole increment-numbering authority and contains one coherent Increment 0-10 sequence. Release 0 is clearly distinguished from risk tier R0, and R0-R4 are otherwise used consistently.
The authority table separates protected contract ownership, approval custody, human issuance, runtime validation, actuator authority, durable facts, external resources, and disposable execution.
All checked local Markdown links and named repository paths resolve. The plan defines future entry/exit evidence rather than claiming those gates passed.

findings.title: The claimed total state projection still maps declared improvement transitions to illegal canonical edges
findings.requirement: R-08/P-08 and the claimed closure of STATE-R2-001 and R2-RJ-001 require every private edge to map to a legal canonical edge, a stutter, or an explicitly guarded ordered canonical transition sequence without skipping READY, LEASED, verification, outcome, rollback verification, or cleanup.
reproduction: Apply the explicit candidate sequence in PLAN section 8.4 to the section 14.0 IMPROVEMENT mapping. CURATION_PASSED -> OFFLINE_PENDING projects VERIFYING -> READY, and OFFLINE_PASSED -> SHADOW_PENDING also projects VERIFYING -> READY. Neither is a legal edge or stutter in the canonical lifecycle.

Apply the explicit rollout sequence CANARY_READY -> CANARY_RUNNING. It projects READY -> OBSERVING, bypassing LEASED and intervening canonical work phases. The row lists LEASED but the declared rollout sequence contains no edge through it.
Section 14.0 permits a private edge to emit intermediate canonical events only when those ordered events and each guard are specified. No such per-edge expansion is supplied for these transitions.
findings.impact: Increment 1 cannot derive the promised graph-valid fixture from the normative plan without inventing transitions. An implementer can either reject the built-in improvement factory or silently bypass admission and lifecycle gates. This leaves two prior high findings incompletely closed and permits an unsafe or undefined implementation.
findings.recommendation: Publish the transition-level mapping, not only a state lookup. Route each mutating rollout through an explicit private LEASED/admission edge and specify every ordered canonical event and guard for multi-phase projections. Add a table or generated fixture proving every declared candidate, rollout, attempt, and control-health edge maps legally.
findings.verification: Enumerating every section 8.4 edge against the mapping yields only canonical legal edges, stutters, or fully listed guarded event sequences, with no READY-to-OBSERVING or VERIFYING-to-READY shortcut.

findings.title: Repository identity remains both optional and mandatory in the supposedly domain-neutral contract
findings.requirement: The claimed closure of CDD-R2-004 and R-15/P-15 require a typed domain ScopeRef and require repository identity only for engineering repository records; a repository ID must not substitute for GTM or other-domain authority.
reproduction: PLAN.md:123 says repository identity is mandatory only for engineering repository records/effects and that the neutral kernel rejects it as a substitute for another domain's authority.
PLAN.md:140 then says each artifact has repository_id without marking it optional or domain-qualified.

PLAN.md:402 more broadly requires every stored, queued, cached, object-stored, and audited record to carry immutable repository_id. This includes the neutral research, decision, identity, and future GTM records described elsewhere.
findings.impact: A schema implementer must either violate the universal artifact/tenant MUSTs or invent repository identities for non-repository scopes. Fake repository binding can become an unsafe authorization substitute, while rejecting it makes the future cross-domain branch unrepresentable. The prior finding is not fully closed.
findings.recommendation: Replace universal repository_id requirements with mandatory tenant_id plus mandatory typed ScopeRef. Require repository_id only when ScopeRef.domain is engineering/repository, with a conditional schema rule that forbids it from satisfying account, consent, campaign, subject, or environment authority in other domains. Apply the same rule to storage, queues, cache keys, audit, and ArtifactRef.
findings.verification: Schema fixtures accept a valid non-repository ResearchArtifact/GTM proposal without repository_id, require repository_id for an engineering repository artifact, and reject cross-domain authorization based only on repository_id.

findings.title: Linked evidence artifacts still assert the unverified pre-cutoff retrieval history that the repair disclaims
findings.requirement: EVID-R2-001 was claimed addressed by treating the cutoff only as intended scope and making no unsupported UTC collection-history assertion.
reproduction: The plan, evidence-repair.md, and research-manifest.json correctly say the legacy corpus does not prove retrieval time and that no re-fetch is claimed.

evidence-index.md nevertheless says 2026-09-13 access dates reflect retrieval performed before the cutoff, and evidence-cutoff.md states that research was executed at approximately 15:00-17:30 UTC. Those are positive collection-history assertions, not merely a convention.
These files remain linked supporting material and are explicitly included in the coverage audit, so a reader encounters two incompatible provenance accounts.
findings.impact: The plan itself fails safe by requiring a fresh immutable re-fetch, so this does not prove an unsafe implementation. It does leave the prior evidence correction editorially incomplete and can cause a reviewer to repeat an unsupported provenance claim.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite evidence-index.md and evidence-cutoff.md to label the timing narrative unverified and non-evidentiary, or archive them under a clearly marked superseded-claims heading. Point all current provenance statements to the manifest disclaimer and PLAN section 4.
findings.verification: A repository-wide search finds no assertion that legacy retrieval occurred before the cutoff; all such dates are labeled unverified local-calendar metadata pending the fresh-run gate.

findings.title: Ordered lists and exact-location citations contain avoidable numbering drift
findings.requirement: A single reader should be able to follow the walkthrough and audit each claimed correction in order.
reproduction: The walkthrough is numbered 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 10, 11. The effect reconciliation outcomes are numbered 1, 3, 4.

The round-2 register labels locations exact but some parenthetical line ranges are stale: ARCH-R2-003 points to PLAN 111-113 although the Release 0 recovery envelope starts at line 117, and SECIMP-R2-006 points to PLAN line 109 although the canonical-principal independence clause is line 99.
findings.impact: No safety gate is bypassed, but sequence references are harder to quote reliably and the exact-location claim is false for some rows.
findings.recommendation: Renumber both lists and replace volatile line-number parentheticals with section heading plus stable clause/table-row names, or regenerate line anchors after final edits.
findings.verification: Both lists are consecutive and every round-2 location resolves to the named clause in the final PLAN.md.

findings.title: The roadmap still instructs the builder to archive prototype artifacts that were removed by design
findings.requirement: The plan-only roadmap and immediate actions should describe executable next actions against the final checkout.
reproduction: README.md says the prototype was removed after its failures were incorporated into the plan.
Increment 0 still says to archive the prototype as non-shipping, and immediate action 3 says to archive or label every prototype schema/model/SQL/CLI artifact. Those artifacts are absent by design.
findings.impact: The first roadmap increment contains a stale, non-executable task. A reader cannot tell whether removal already satisfies it or whether an external archive is required.
findings.recommendation: Change the task to verify and record that prototype product artifacts are absent, while retaining only the review/resolution evidence. If an external archive is required, name its owner, location, contents, and non-authoritative status.
findings.verification: Increment 0 and section 24 describe an action that can be completed from the final plan-only repository and agree with README.md.

residual_uncertainty: This audit did not execute future compilers, model checking, databases, sandboxes, GitHub effects, evidence re-fetches, or pilot gates. The plan correctly leaves all such proof in future increments.
External HTTP content and semantic source entailment were not revalidated. PLAN section 4 correctly blocks implementation pending that work.
Apart from the findings above, all 25 round-2 findings have an identifiable plan-level response; closure cannot pass while CEC-R3-001 and CEC-R3-002 remain open.
